text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I like the size of the pieces because I have kids in my home who like legos and with those it can be hard to find pieces because they are so small and they end up all over the place. I also like the color combination that was provided. The instructions have to be accessed through a website, which is okay, but I would have liked to have paper directions (but that's just a personal preference).

What I like: 1) within the app it provides step by step directions to build the characters. You have to press play through each step therefore you move along at your own pace. You can also flip the image around so you can see the sides, front, and bottom of the chracter (how it should be) so you can make sure everything is in the right spot. 2) the pieces are very sturdy. I don't forsee myself having a problem with them breaking unless its intentional. 3) it charges really quickly. The block that is the main piece of the entire item is rechargeable. After playing with it for sometime the battery indicated it was on 17% (through the app) and it only took about 20 minutes to fully charge.

What I didn't like: 1) the app is a pain. The description states the item is optimized for android devices with android 7.0 or more, but this is not true. I have three tablets and a samsung chromebook with android 7.0 or more, but when I go to the appstore, it says the app is not optimized for my device or I cannot find the app at all. I had to download the app on my Galaxy S9. Which I would rather the kids be able to play with it on their own devices instead of my phone. I also added it to an iphone XR and it worked. 2) the app isn't the best functionally. It would shut off on me randomly or freeze up. It even caused my phone to go black for about five minutes and after plugging it into the charger and waiting, it finally popped up on camera mode. 3) it is not always easy or fast getting the phone and the item to connect. You have to have your location and bluetooth on and even when the device is powered on, the app will tell you to power it on. Then half the time, it takes 3-5 minutes to finally connect. 4) I like to coding part, because you can do an order of functions, but when you want to just play with it, you can only go back and forth or right and left, depending on the character you built. We built an alligator and it just opened and closed its mouth and not with the same force each time.

Overall, It's a nice toy, but I would not purchase it for $99
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

text_fidelity_a:
Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens I generally don't prefer electronic learning, but these are pretty cool. The Smart Letters each have three rubber feet that are spaced differently, and the tablet recognizes the letter when you gently place it on the tablet screen. It took about 10 minutes to download all 6 free apps (3 for letters, 3 for numbers) and to set up the quick profile. The apps are simple to use and well designed. Next is a summary of the 3 letter apps:

Bla Bla Box: spell out words and hear them read back to you
Alphamonster: choose a letter to hear the sound the letter makes and see a picture of a word beginning with that letter. See a picture of an item and identify what letter the item starts with. Hear a sound of a letter and identify the letter. See a cursive lowercase letter and identity the matching wooden uppercase letter. (In the settings you can pick which letters will appear throughout these challenges. The default is the entire alphabet but you can pick just a few if your child needs to focus on certain letters)
Vocabubble: game 1- pick any letter and as you repeatedly place the letter on the tablet, 8 different pictures of items beginning with that letter will fall down the screen. Game 2 - choose two letters, then pictures of items beginning with those two letters will fall down the screen and you tap the picture with the right letter in order for it to disappear. (This was a fun game my niece and nephew enjoyed playing together as they each held a letter. However, some pictures seemed too hard or random for a 5 year old, such as an Orca for the letter O... kids will think it's a Whale... or a Totem Pole or Quaill, etc)

My five year old niece and nephew enjoyed testing these for me and were definitely interested in the games. I'm excited to start my daughter with it when she turns three and I can see the number apps extending the usefulness of the product as she gets older. Four stars, not five, only because they do seem a bit pricey and also because the accent on the American English setting we tried out is a bit odd at times.
text_fidelity_b: Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens

text_fidelity_a:
IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens What a great creative art toy. You can do literally anything with this and takes your sketches off the paper and into three dimensions. I am amazed at the ways the kids put this into practice, and it kept them engrossed for hours with only a couple squabbles over people hogging this color or that. I'll get more into what we did below. But first, What you get and How this works.

This product is a hardening gel that can be squeezed into shapes using plastic forms. There are several forms that come with the kit, a flat sheet of plastic and a couple rounded forms for creating spherical shapes. The flat clear piece is great for tracing images so even young kids can achieve the shapes they desire. Also, we used it to make other curves to help flesh out animal shapes, but that proved a little more difficult.

Once you have drawn your shapes with one of the gel pens, you can use the UV flashlight to harden the pieces to make them retain the shapes you want. Then you can peel them off the plastic forms or sheet and cement elements together into three dimensional structures. The possibilities are endless and only limited by creativity. Our kids started out by tracing the provided dinosaurs and moved on to tracing other dinos from various books until they had a small forest of dinos and trees.

Warnings and caveats: I'm a little leery of the chemically nature of this toy. There are warnings to avoid skin contact in light. This put me a little on edge and I wanted to supervise our 8 through 14 year olds to make sure it was not getting on skin or other stuff. Also, this does take a bit of artistic ability. It can be as free form as you want it to be, but we did have some frustration when younger kids could not recreate the stuff the older kids were building. But for the most part it was very conducive to creativity.

Also, the end products are a little sticky. So they don't seem like you can play with your creations, but you can make wonderful visual art. We have a nice little dino diorama on our book shelf now and the kids seem pretty proud of it. The inks are also a little messy, so make sure your in a cleanable area.

Personally, I think this is one of the most wonderfully novel and creative ideas I've seen in a while. I will be picking up some for the kids on my Christmas list, and look forward to refilling our supply.
text_fidelity_b: IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

text_fidelity_a:
2-Axis Gimbal GPS EIS Drones with Camera for Adults 4K, Long Range Transmission, Auto Return Home Follow Me, DEERC Quadcopter with 2 Modular Batteries 52 Mins, Level 5 Wind Resistance, Brushless Motor [[VIDEOID:6bc966f8fe8fd5a07ab64de80c7d0bb7]] This is my first drone and I can say I was very impressed. I have only had it up a couple times due to bad weather and my work schedule. I watched a couple videos and away I went. The instructions are very simple although there is a lot to learn. I’m still in the learning process but so far I love it. It is so easy. It’s almost idiot proof. I had it up for about four minutes my first flight and I was very nervous. My second flight was so much fun and I was more comfortable but I still don’t want to try taking a video just yet. I did make one but I did not have the camera angle straight. I’ll post a video if the weather holds out this weekend. I will say if you are thinking about which drone to get, this one is perfect for beginners or someone with some experience. It takes beautiful photos and videos and it is so stable. I can’t say enough about how much I enjoyed the time I have used it. With no doubt, I would buy it again. If you purchase one, you won’t regret it. Thanks Deerc for the great product……. Oh and I did hit a tree limb and it did not phase it. No damage at all.
Update. Had time to take it up today. 1/7/2023. I’m convinced that this is almost idiot proof. You can fly it in to objects but just make sure you are in an open area. I sat it in the middle of my concrete driveway and hit the take off button and it took off. I got the nerve to change the flight parameters in the settings. I changed it to the max height and distance. I didn’t record a video in this mode but I took it up 300 feet and to a distance of 4000 feet from the controller. I could barely see it. Got very scared and thought I might lose it so I hit the home button. Within 10 seconds she was back in clear view. The views are amazing. I didn’t know there were so many interesting things around my house. I can’t wait to take it to my office and take some videos of my dealership. After this flight, I can say I’d definitely buy it again. I’ve never had so much fun without leaving my driveway. So again, get you one. Thanks Deerc.
text_fidelity_b: 2-Axis Gimbal GPS EIS Drones with Camera for Adults 4K, Long Range Transmission, Auto Return Home Follow Me, DEERC Quadcopter with 2 Modular Batteries 52 Mins, Level 5 Wind Resistance, Brushless Motor

Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers - Educational Wooden Pattern Blocks Playset in Vehicle Transportation Shapes with Vibrant Colors, 5 Brain-Building Peg Puzzles Youngsters have special educational needs. They love to play and as parents, we want to give them things to play with that also exercise their young, curious, developing minds. A good toy for this purpose is this Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar.

Packaged in a box, this set contains 6 different dinosaur puzzles and each of the puzzles has just 6 pieces. The puzzles are each assembled on a small board measuring about 7 by 6 inches. The small size makes the puzzles just right for young kids and the bright colors are certain to get a child’s attention.

With only 6 pieces, toddlers are the age group most likely to benefit from these puzzles. Kids have a chance to show their skill as they put each of the pieces into place. Depending on a child’s interest and skill level, some may take longer than others, but most preschool age kids will be determined to assemble and show off their completed puzzle to supportive parents.

With all these pieces, there could be a tendency to lose them, but fortunately, the manufacturer includes a storage bag. You could place them back into the box, but the storage bag is better. It’s cool that the manufacturer thought to add this because it’s practical and better ensures that pieces don’t get lost.

Teaching problem- solving skills to young people can be accomplished in many ways and a toy like the Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar is useful for this purpose. With 6 puzzles and just 6 pieces each, a young person can complete each with relative ease and improve coordination and other skills in the process.
text_fidelity_b: Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers - Educational Wooden Pattern Blocks Playset in Vehicle Transportation Shapes with Vibrant Colors, 5 Brain-Building Peg Puzzles

CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver [[VIDEOID:a47326bb48b328d18558c86fcccc38a1]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very high quality. The handle alone is 12.4 ounces.
* USB-C charging port.
* Belt clip included.
* Decorative blade plug is included. This is cool if you just want to display the handle without the blade. You can cap off your handle with this decorative plug.
* Bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap instead of a pommel/coupling.
* Hilt is 1-1/4 inch. This will connect with other 1.25 inch handles to create a duo saber. Another dominant size on the market is a smaller 1 and 1/8th diameter version. This one will not thread onto 1.25 hilts, so to create duo sabers with different brands, be sure the hilts are the same size.
* All the special effects are pretty much standard: Lock up effect, changing colors, steady, pulse, unstable, etc. This version also has quotes. Watch my video to see a demo

THE BAD:
------------
* Pommel or coupling is not included. As mentioned above, bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap. When you remove this speaker cap, the bottom of this hilt will be male. So to create the duo saber, your other saber should have a coupling so that it's female.
* My light saber did not charge properly out the box. When you plug it in to charge, it'll loudly announce, "Charging!" Then the red light will blink slowly. When it is complete, it will say, "READY," and the red light will be stable, no blinking. Chances are you're not going to be present when the saber says READY. But as long as you see the red light is stable and not blinking, then you'll know it's fully charged. My issue was that after 10 hrs of charging, the red light was still blinking slowly, and the saber wouldn't turn on. I contacted customer support and they had a solution ready to go. So this seems like a common problem. I talk about this at the end of my video, so watch it if you have a charging issue. My saber is charging properly now. So the word to describe this saber is, finicky.

I'll give this an overall rating of 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver

Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor I am overall satisfied with my order of the Simba Steffi Love Camper Set. This arrived very well packaged for shipping. It was not overly difficult to remove from the box as most of the securing straps simply untied. There were several pieces of clear tape that needed to be removed. I do like that this set included a Steffi Love doll. It's an overall nice doll with articulated ankles and knees. I do wish that the elbows were also articulated, but they are not. She has shoes, a simple dress and sunglasses. She has underpants imprinted on her plastic pelvis. I do not advise to remove the elastic on her hair as the plugged hair will show the widely spaced hair plugs and be less than attractive.

The first impression of the playset inside the packaging is that it's very cute and attractive. The camper itself is not as durable as I had hoped. This will not stand up to rough play. I would not at all advise this to be accessible to toddlers or careless children because if one tried to use it as a seat or step-stool, it would break easily. The wheels are held in place with a metal rod, this would be a safety hazard if it came out of place. The many small accessories are also not appropriate for very small children as they could pose a choking hazard. There is not enough leg room in the two front seats for the doll's legs, they must be bent to the side or the doll has to sit sideways. Not all of the doors are well-molded to close completely. Some stickers are included, which is nice as one side of the camper already is decorated with stickers, leaving the opposite side blank. Several packets of accessories are included so the dolls can use props for various activities such as cooking, lounging and even showering. The small accessories are the best point of this playset.

I personally do not find this camper set to be a good value at it's current price point. There are too many issues that will lead to frustration in play. Primarily, the type of plastic material used to mold the camper is prone to failure as it's not at all durable. The play patterns of most small children will prove to be the source of frustration or failure of the toy. This type of plastic is prone to shattering and can produce sharp edges if broken. For many children, this will be a short-lived disposable toy. This would be most ideal for children that play gently and are able to keep small toys well organized and enjoy playing with fashion dolls. The camper itself measures about 22" long, 11" wide and 9 1/2" tall. This will need a significant amount of storage space, and would not easily withstand being stored stacked with other toys in a toybox. This would be best 'parked' under a bed, in a closet or on a shelf between play sessions to avoid a tripping hazard. I hope that my experience with this camper set is helpful as you kindly click the button below.
text_fidelity_b: Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor

Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds This recycling truck is awesome. It takes two AA batteries (included for demonstration purposes only—meaning they may have to be replaced using a Phillips screwdriver shortly after use). The biggest difficulty I had is in removing this truck from the box because it arrives in the ON condition and started working immediately as I was trying to unpack it. That was a bit annoying.

The on / off button is located underneath the truck under the cab. There are two levels of sound and lights to choose from when turning on.

Once the truck is on, the button in the center of the CAB turns on the ignition sounds and the lights come on.

The lights also come on when pressing down on the tires and moving forward and backward. When moving backward, the backup warning sounds activate.

The recycling truck container opens in back and can store Legos or other small toys. It also tilts back to the rear.

All the sounds of dumping, loading, and idling are realistic. Pressing down on the horns on either side of the cab also generates realistic sounds.

The recycling bucket has a slot that allows for placement into the hitch. Once in place, move the lever handle down to dump (or pretend dump) what is in the pail. The pail can also be stored in the top of the truck’s container.

The instructions are useless as it only talks about the batteries. Therefore, it is important to pay attention to the pictures on the box or read the description on Amazon to learn how to fully operate this vehicle. Another option is to learn via trial and error.

To me this is an extremely impressive toy for a reasonable price of $29.99.
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Cars, Large-Scale, 15-in Toy Recycling Truck with Garbage Bin, Lights and Sounds

2021 Smart Watches for Women, Fitness Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Blood Oxygen Monitor, IP68 Waterproof Activity Tracker with Pedometer, Smartwatch for Android Phones I've been on the search for a smartwatch that meets all my needs. I'd like to find one that has a small watch face, bands that can be changed, uses a good app, and can monitor O2, sleep, and a wide variety of exercise. This watch was a perfect 10 in looking nice for my small wrists, and bands that can be changed. Unfortunately it fell quite short of the mark for everything else I needed.

The app has me ready to put this watch back in the box and try something else. It's a really clunky app compared to others I've tried (Fitbit, Da Fit). The exercise feature is very limiting and doesn't account for any indoor exercise like a stationary bike, aerobics, treadmill, etc. Most of the time the steps on the app are wrong compared to the steps on the watch, even after trying to sync it again. It's disappointing that there's so few watch faces to choose from. I can't even choose the screen analog look watch face that is displayed on the box, it's not an option on the app at all. The O2 feature is nice, and so is the sleep feature. I do hope they'll continue to work on the app, it does have potential but doesn't work well for me as it is right now.

I'm also having some trouble trying to use the long press on the watch itself to select features. It's just not working no matter how often I try. It's really disappointing that such a beautiful watch has so many problems. I would have really liked to use it as my main watch, but my search will have to continue on.

The problem is that all of the mechanisms are so flimsy that it’s just not a good toy for the age it is meant for. They get frustrated when things don’t work and don’t understand why things don’t work when they take the correct action. Add to that the helicopter mechanism not working at all because it’s too far away from the car, and you just can’t enjoy the toy.

So I mentioned the helicopter doesn’t work. It’s too high for the magnet to grab the car. So your 2 or 3 year old won’t understand at all why one of the knobs doesn’t work. Then the car gets to the bridge, which at least works most often. Then the grey lifting part which constantly comes out of its socket. Then the area where the cars turn…if you aren’t slow and gentle the cars will get bumped off the track. Everything is just so flimsy.

Due to all the issues, as an adult it’s impossible to get a single car all the way through the circuit, even when being as careful as possible. So there’s no way a child can possibly make it happen. Don’t get me wrong, my kid is still playing with it but she doesn’t use any of the buttons or levers…just kinda pushes the cars around the ramp (which comes off every single time she moves the toy)

2 stars because my toddler is enjoying the toy, despite all of its flaws. But none of the things it claims to do…are happening. We will trash this toy in about a week or two.

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS The MACTANO Starry Night Building Kit is a micro brick set, so it’s not compatible with regular size building sets. And the bricks really are micro! I don’t recommend this set for kids or anyone with dexterity issues. Many of the pieces are smaller than the tip of a q-tip.

I’ve been building sets for three decades, and I’ll be honest, this one was a big challenge. Patience and attention to detail are extremely necessary. I keep looking at my finished set and noticing mistakes I made, or steps I missed.

The pieces do stay together, very important for an off-brand set. The kit includes a tiny brick separator, it’s cute and much needed.

If I have so much experience, why did I find this set so difficult? First, each step in the instructions is really 2 to 5 steps. For example, step 12 uses over sixty(!) pieces to put together four rows of the backdrop. Every step is like that, and you have to pay extremely close attention to figure out what pieces go where.

Second, sometimes it wasn’t clear what color to use or where a piece should go, but I couldn’t look ahead. Future steps greyed out the colors for previous steps, and sometimes didn’t show the complete build, part of it would be cut off.

Third, some of the colors are very hard to tell apart. I used the wrong shade of blue multiple times, but I quit caring. Most of the painting is blue, so only I know about those mistakes. But for the very dark blue and very dark green, it’s hard to see the outlines of the individual pieces in the instructions.

I build brick sets to relax. Working on this set was the opposite of relaxing for me, since I had to focus so much.
text_fidelity_b: MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS

text_fidelity_a:
Blue Orange Ring It! The Clap & Ring Game I love games that can manage parity across many ages. This is a lot like Spot it in that regards, where a 7 year old can compete fairly well with a 47 year old once everyone knows what they are looking for. The reaching for the bell is kinetic enough to engage kids to make them want to be the first to slam the ringer, and the rules are so easy they can immediately be digested. The action is fast and again engaging, and we had a lot of laughs with the came, and surprisingly few injuries and fights.

The game in its simplest form is almost too easy, but it lends itself to more and more levels of complexity. There are three variables, numbers, color (8 or more) and a shape. You can play complex combos like match a shape and a number, or two numbers must add up to ten and there needs to be a match. Instant ring it and visually similar don't ring it cards cause quick victories as well as quick penalties.

This is a perfect game to pull out for some quick games. The container holds all the pieces and makes it wonderfully portable. The parts are decent quality and I expect it to hold up well.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Ring It! The Clap & Ring Game

Also the face and hair of this doll are more true to Gal Gadot, the actress who played the part, so some of the magic of the movie is captured. As she comes she is HARDLY "Battle Ready!" Comes with decent quality carrying case that stores everything perfectly, along with a zippered compartment area, where you can keep the manuals and spare props, yes you get a set free with the drone!

Flies well in the wind I put it up in winds that were around 15-18 mph and it handled them well, of course the advertised battery life suffered and was only about 17 minutes but it was fighting the wind the whole time. On a less windy day it was almost 24 minutes of total flight time!

If your looking for a drone to learn on at a decent price point this is a good one and it's the right size, this is my 3rd Holy stone drone and I'm pleased with the product, I own the 700d, 270, and now this bad boy. All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!
